title: Business Development Manager
description: The opportunity Total Delivery Pharma is growing, and we are looking for a commercially ambitious Business Development Manager to help us reach more organisations across the pharmaceutical and wider life-sciences sectors. This is an opportunity to take real ownership of business development within a specialist consultancy. You will have an established CRM and leads to work from, alongside the freedom to develop new relationships, test new approaches and build a strong pipeline of your own. We are not looking for someone who only books meetings and hands opportunities over. We want somebody who enjoys opening doors, understanding what matters to a prospective client and staying with the opportunity through discovery, proposal, negotiation and decision. About TDP TDP provides pharmaceutical quality, compliance and regulatory consultancy to clients in the UK and internationally. Our services include QP and RP support, GxP auditing, regulatory affairs, CMC and MS&T, batch review, compliance remediation, training, due diligence and outsourced quality and regulatory functions. Our clients come to us when they need experienced, practical support with important and often time-sensitive challenges. You do not need to be a technical consultant, but you will need the curiosity and confidence to learn our services, ask strong questions and communicate their commercial value clearly. What you will do Use HubSpot to identify, prioritise and develop leads and target accounts. Create new opportunities through thoughtful outreach, referrals, networking, partnerships, events and inbound enquiries. Lead discovery conversations and understand the client's need, urgency, stakeholders, budget, decision process and timescale. Build trusted relationships with senior decision-makers across pharmaceutical and life-sciences organisations. Position TDP's services clearly and turn technical capability into relevant commercial value. Qualify opportunities properly and focus time on work with a genuine route to decision. Coordinate the input needed to develop clear, commercially sound proposals while retaining ownership of the client relationship. Present proposals, manage follow-up, handle objections and negotiate within agreed authority. Maintain a clean and accurate pipeline, with clear next steps and reliable forecasts. Support a structured handover when work is won so the client experience remains strong from sale into delivery. What we are looking for A proven track record in outbound B2B business development or consultative service sales. Experience progressing opportunities beyond an introductory meeting and contributing directly to a commercial decision. Confidence selling high-value or complex services to senior stakeholders. Strong discovery, qualification, relationship-building, follow-up and negotiation skills. Comfort using a CRM to manage activity, pipeline and forecasts. HubSpot experience would be particularly useful. Commercial awareness, including an understanding of pricing, margin and the difference between activity and genuine progress. The ability to learn a technical service offering and explain it in clear, practical language. A self-starting and persistent approach, combined with sound judgement and honest forecasting. Experience that would be helpful Experience in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medical devices, scientific services, laboratories, CROs, CDMOs or another regulated professional-services market would be valuable, but it is not essential. We are equally interested in strong service-sales professionals who can show that they learn quickly, ask intelligent questions and take ownership of a complex commercial process. What you will get A supportive and collaborative workplace where people share knowledge and work together. A visible role with meaningful ownership of your pipeline, relationships and results. A company that is keen to encourage development and help its people succeed. The opportunity to build your knowledge of the pharmaceutical and life-sciences sectors while developing as an independent seller of complex services. Uncapped commission and clear scope to increase your earnings through performance. Private healthcare, life insurance, income protection and a company pension. Remote working, with opportunities to meet clients and represent TDP at relevant industry events. Your development We want the successful person to become confident and increasingly independent in the role. You will receive support while you learn TDP's services and market, with the expectation that you will progressively take ownership of discovery, qualification, proposals, negotiation and closing. We will encourage you to build your capability, contribute ideas and shape how TDP approaches business development as the company grows. Success in this role should create scope for greater responsibility, stronger earnings and continued career development. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Treasury Lead
location: London or remote within the UK
description: About Griffin Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences. We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more. We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies. Learn more about what we do Our culture We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible. We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life. We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified. Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers. Learn more about our culture. The Team Our vision is that our Finance team plays a central part of the business, somewhere the Board can rely on to support strategic planning. In this our treasury team keeps us safely funded and liquid and gives the Board and ALCO numbers they can trust. As we add products and markets, the team is growing. As second hire to the team, you’ll report directly to our Treasurer, sitting at the heart of how we capture, report, analyse and manage risk to support how we optimise Griffin’s balance sheet. The opportunity Treasury at a fintech bank is different. You’ll see real-time payment flows and deposit behaviour that a conventional bank never sees. You’ll work directly with our Treasurer to build our treasury processes, reporting and systems rather than inherit them. You’ll contribute to management of liquidity as a Direct FPS participant, use of facilities within the Bank of England’s Sterling Monetary Framework (SMF), card issuing and stablecoin infrastructure. What success looks like By month 3, you’ll understand our business and processes, run daily reporting with Michael’s review and handle daily cash positioning, including our Bank of England reserve account. By month 6, you’ll own daily and monthly reporting and run intraday cash management independently, including testing the SMF. You’ll have drafted ALCO papers and credit reviews, delivered your first automation improvements and contributed to the impact assessment for Direct FPS or a similar product launch. To do this you’ll own Daily and intraday reporting on liquidity, capital, interest rate risk, funding capacity and asset encumbrance, with every output sense-checked before it goes out Risk monitoring against our risk appetite: limits, triggers and early warning indicators, forecast-versus-actual reviews, and stress tests you design with the Treasurer Intraday cash management and liquidity forecasting: cash positioning, payments and transfers, depositor behaviour and outflow assumptions Monthly management reporting, including interest income, margin and customer profitability, the ALCO pack, inputs to regulatory returns, and contributions to the ILAAP and ICAAP Dealing operations: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations, settlements and collateral movements, plus credit analysis on counterparties and issuers. You’ll also cover for the Treasurer with brokers, treasury bill auctions and SMF drawdowns Automating manual steps, closing control gaps, and documenting procedures that mean knowledge never sits with just two people Maintaining our treasury bank and broker mandates We expect you to shape this role This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are. Your background To succeed in the role, we're looking for people who have: 5+ years in a bank treasury function (e.g. middle-office, ALM or balance sheet management), measuring and reporting liquidity and capital from economic and regulatory perspectives. You will have produced reports hands-on rather than reviewed them Strong prudential knowledge across liquidity, capital and leverage (e.g. CRR, Basel III, LCR, NSFR, IRRBB, ILAAP, ICAAP), and hands-on exposure to the dealing lifecycle: pre- and post-trade checks, confirmations and settlements Advanced Excel skills (e.g. data tables, scenario analysis, VBA), plus the attention to detail and reconciliation discipline to sense-check everything you produce An analytical, inquisitive mindset, with a habit of automating what’s manual The organisation and drive to work autonomously, remotely and asynchronously, and the appetite for the breadth and ambiguity of building in an early-stage bank A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write ) Ideally, you would also: Hold a treasury or accountancy qualification (ACT, CertBALM, FRM, CFA, ACA, ACCA or CIMA) Bring Python, SQL, Power BI or AI skills Knowledge of Direct FPS and Bank of England SMF facilities Experience implementing or using treasury or ALM systems What can we offer you? Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year Time off: 28 days’ holiday + bank holidays Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment. As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks. How long will the process take? We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other. Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience. Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements. Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin. Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview. Step 5 : Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here . How do I apply? Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next. We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs. Under representation At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

executive leadership Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC) Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop title: Sr. AI/ML Engineer (MXC)
description: Do work that matters. At AlertMedia , we help organizations protect their people, operations, and brand. Our modern Risk Intelligence and Response platform empowers teams to detect emerging threats, assess impact, and respond with confidence. We believe building resilience should be simpler—and it starts with bringing critical information and workflows together in one unified platform. Our core values drive us in our important mission of keeping people safe & informed: We’re humans not robots Customers always come first We work better together Simplicity is our strength Our reputation is priceless Hard work pays off AlertMedia is looking for an innovative and hands-on Sr. AI/ML Engineer with a strong background in applied machine learning and data science to lead the evaluation, training, and integration of advanced AI and machine learning models across our product suite. You will have the opportunity to show who you are throughout our interview process; we don’t ask any trick questions or expect you to perform a whiteboard exercise. We want to see you shine by showing us work you are most proud of! You’re a collaborative engineer who thrives in a fast-moving environment, and you’re as comfortable training and fine-tuning models as you are crafting prompts or evaluating model outputs. You have a strong understanding of ML fundamentals, but you're pragmatic in applying the right solution for the problem. What you get to do every day: Train and fine-tune supervised learning models (e.g., classification, ranking, embeddings) for internal tools and customer-facing product features. Lead prompt engineering and testing efforts to fine-tune LLM behavior for specific use cases across the product suite. Design and implement evaluation pipelines for both LLMs and traditional ML models. Work with and optimize Elasticsearch-backed data systems that power AI and intelligence pipelines. Proactively identify opportunities to improve AI models, data pipelines, and engineering workflows beyond the existing roadmap. Develop tools and frameworks to support prompt iteration, model benchmarking, and performance tracking. Coordinate with security team to ensure adherence to AI compliance standards. Evaluate and compare commercial and open-source LLMs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Meta, etc.) for performance, cost, alignment, and reliability. Collaborate with product and engineering teams to integrate AI features in a safe, scalable, and maintainable way. Monitor, evaluate, and continuously improve the performance of AI and machine learning models in production. Stay informed of emerging research in NLP, machine learning, and AI infrastructure, and evaluate potential applications for the business. title: Senior IT & Corporate Engineering
description: Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners . We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners. Since launching publicly in September 2023 , Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue , with a clear path to profitability by late 2026 . We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership. Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue) —the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved. Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt. - Mission-critical problems : We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale. - High bar, low ego : Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership. - Speed over comfort : We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results. - Enduring impact : What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses. Team & Locations We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote. Flex Fuels Ambition. About The Role This role owns IT and corporate engineering at Flex, end to end. It reports directly to the CTO. We think IT's job is enablement. The measure of this function is not how many tickets it closes or how many controls it can point at. It is whether everyone else at Flex can do their work faster and more safely than they could last quarter. A new hire productive on day one instead of day four. An engineer who gets exactly the access they need in minutes, without asking twice and without being handed the keys to everything. A team that can adopt a new tool because someone reviewed it properly, not because they routed around IT to buy it on a personal card. So we are not looking for a gatekeeper, or for someone whose default answer is no. The right person makes the safe path the easy path, and removes friction permanently instead of absorbing it repeatedly. Which is why this role also owns Flex's corporate security posture. Identity, access, endpoints, and the SaaS estate are one system, and the person who makes access fast should be the person who decides how much access is reasonable. Split those across two teams and employees route around both. You'll set conditional access and MFA policy, own privileged access and endpoint posture, and run third-party OAuth and Workspace grant review. Our security engineers own the product and infrastructure side, the money paths and the code, and you'll work with them constantly. Corporate security is yours to decide, not to implement on someone else's behalf. This is the hard part of the job, and we'd rather say so than leave it as a bonus line. The argument between moving fast and holding a line is now an argument you have with yourself. Day to day, what gets tightened, what gets mitigated, and what we knowingly accept is your call; the large ones come to the CTO, and we'd rather see a close call early than find out you decided it quietly. What we'd ask is that a no comes from a real read of the risk and the business context rather than a standard applied by default. The rest of the work has two halves. The IT half is the fleet, identity, access, the SaaS estate, and the joiner/mover/leaver process, delivered with help from a managed IT partner who handles procurement, device logistics, tier-1 support, and international coverage. You own that relationship, define the SLA, and enforce it. The corporate engineering half is the part we think makes this a good job: writing the automation and internal tooling that means the IT half doesn't scale linearly with headcount. If a process only works because a person runs it by hand every Tuesday, we'd rather you replaced it. You'd be inheriting an estate here, not starting one. The first year is as much untangling what has already accumulated - stale access, tools nobody reviewed, processes that work because someone remembers them - as it is building what comes next. Automate that assessment. Nobody should be reading through a SaaS estate by hand in 2026. Now the shape of this. Flex is around 150 people, and you would be the only person in this function, with vendor capacity underneath you and a direct line to the CTO. That means real autonomy and real scope from week one. It also means this is a hands-on senior individual contributor role, not a management role, and we are not planning a team under it in the near term. If you're looking to build and lead an IT organization right now, this isn't that job, and we'd rather you knew before you applied. We're looking for an IT and corporate engineering builder who wants to own security posture, rather than a security specialist willing to cover IT. Both halves have to interest you. If the enablement work reads as the price of admission for the security work, this will be a frustrating job. What You'll Do Own IT and corporate engineering end to end: the roadmap, the budget, the vendor relationships, and the outcomes. Manage our external IT partner as delivery capacity, not as a peer function. Define the scope, set the SLA, hold them to it, and own the escalation path when it slips. Design the joiner, mover, and leaver process and the entitlement model behind it. Make onboarding fast enough that a new hire is working on day one, and keep deprovisioning in-house and same-day, because it's the highest-consequence action in IT. Administer and improve our identity and productivity stack (Okta, Google Workspace, and the SaaS estate around them), including SSO, SCIM, and group and role design. Own operational policy: device standards, the access-request workflow, and SaaS onboarding and procurement review. Review tools before people buy them, and make that review fast enough that nobody wants to skip it. Build the automation. Provisioning, access reviews, asset and license reconciliation, and the internal tooling that removes recurring manual work across the SaaS estate. Run the endpoint and MDM program across a distributed, increasingly international company, and keep the fleet in a state you'd be comfortable showing an auditor. Own Flex's corporate security posture. Conditional access, MFA, session and device rules, and privileged access are yours to set. So is endpoint posture, and the review of third-party OAuth and Workspace grants that quietly accumulate at every company this age. Design and deliver the security awareness and training program. Not a once-a-year video, and not the version people click through with the sound off. Partner with our security engineers, who own product and infrastructure security. The line runs between corporate and product, not between operating and deciding. You'll bring them into identity decisions with blast radius, and they'll rely on you for provisioning data they can trust. Work closely with People, Finance, and Legal. Onboarding, offboarding, spend, and audit evidence all run through this function. Be a real internal service. Publish what you own, respond when people ask, and find the friction before it turns into a workaround. What Makes You A Great Fit You think IT exists to make other people effective, and you can point at specific friction you removed rather than tickets you closed. You write code. Not necessarily production services, but scripts, integrations, and glue that other people end up depending on. You'd rather fix the process than get faster at the workaround. You hold both sides of this honestly. You've said no to something that mattered, and you've also said yes to something a stricter version of you would have blocked, and you can explain both calls. You're comfortable being the only person in a function, and comfortable saying what you need instead of quietly absorbing it. You know you can't be in the loop on every request, and you don't want to be. You build the self-service paths that let people get what they need without going through you. You can hold a vendor accountable without turning the relationship adversarial. You can tell a colleague, including a senior one, that what they've built can't keep the access it has, explain why in plain language, and work alongside them to find a way that works. You're calm when something is broken and several people are watching. You explain technical constraints clearly to people who don't share your background, in writing, across time zones. What We're Looking For Substantial hands-on experience owning IT or corporate engineering at a growing company, including a stretch where you were the most senior person doing the work. Roughly [6+] years is typical, but we care about what you've owned, not the year count. Deep, hands-on ownership of an identity provider (Okta, Entra, JumpCloud, or similar) at the design layer: SSO, SCIM, SAML, group and entitlement modeling. Not just the admin console. Practical experience running Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 as a platform. Real MDM and endpoint experience across macOS, and ideally Windows, in a remote or hybrid company. Automation ability in at least one scripting or programming language (Python, Go, TypeScript, or similar), and comfort with APIs and identity plumbing. Experience designing an access model and running access reviews, not only fulfilling requests. Real ownership of identity security decisions, not only their execution. You've set MFA or conditional access policy, tightened privileged access, or cleaned up third-party app grants, and you can talk about what you traded away to do it. Track record managing an outsourced IT provider or MSP, or a clear-eyed view of why the ones you've worked with succeeded or failed. Clear written communication. Much of this job is asynchronous and cross-team. Strongly Preferred Experience in a regulated or audited environment (SOC 2, PCI, or a bank partnership), as the control owner rather than the auditor. Time as the senior security voice somewhere without a security team, or without a CISO to escalate to. Experience supporting employees and contractors across multiple countries, including device logistics and local employment platforms. Experience at a company that grew quickly enough that you had to replace your own early processes. Experience introducing AI tooling internally in a way that was actually adopted and actually governed. Interested? We'd love to hear from you At Flex, we value passion, determination, and honesty. Even if you don't fully match the job specifics, we encourage you to apply. Unusual career paths and unique skills can help you stand out. We believe diversity drives our success. Join us at jobs@flex.one Flex is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital or family status, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we'll sort it out. Compensation Final compensation within this range will be based on experience, qualifications, and interview performance. This position is also eligible for equity compensation. Flex offers medical, dental and vision insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) plan. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Additional Informa

title: Director of Security Operations and Engineering
description: A Little About Us EDB provides a data and AI platform that enables organizations to harness the full power of Postgres for transactional, analytical, and AI workloads across any cloud, anywhere. EDB empowers enterprises to control risk, manage costs and scale efficiently for a data and AI led world. Serving more than 1,500 customers globally and as the leading contributor to the vibrant and fast-growing PostgreSQL community, EDB supports major government organizations, financial services, media and information technology companies. EDB’s data-driven solutions enable customers to modernize legacy systems and break data silos while leveraging enterprise-grade open source technologies. EDB delivers the confidence of up to 99.999% high availability with mission critical capabilities built in such as security, compliance controls, and observability. For more information, visit www.enterprisedb.com The Role: You'll lead Security Operations and Security Engineering at EDB, reporting to the CISO as a trusted member of the security leadership team. You own how we detect, respond, and (increasingly) prevent. That means the people, the platforms, and the playbooks behind threat detection, incident response, and the engineering that makes them scale. You'll be a peer to the leaders across security, including Governance, Risk & Compliance and Application Security & Vulnerability Management, and you'll help shape the direction of the broader InfoSec organization. You'll also partner closely with peer leaders in IT and Product, because most of the controls we define live in their systems, pipelines, and roadmaps. This is a scaling role. The business is growing fast, and so is everything security has to cover: more products, more cloud, more acquired companies and environments to bring up to a common standard. You'll decide what to build, what to automate, and where to add people, so the program grows ahead of the risk instead of behind it. As EDB grows, so will the scope and opportunity of the role. One leader owns both Security Operations and Security Engineering on purpose: the best incident is the one that never happens. What we learn from detection and response feeds directly into the engineering of preventive controls, so we move from detecting bad things to making them impossible, and from manual triage to automation and agents that give analysts leverage. If you want to build that, and grow a program and a team as the company grows, this is the seat. What your impact will be: Incident response end to end, from intake and severity model through after-action and improvement, including partnership with Legal on investigations Detection engineering, threat hunting, and the SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and cloud security platforms that support them Security Engineering strategy and delivery, with the goal of preventing incidents rather than responding to them: preventive controls, least privilege, and identity assurance across employees, contractors, and build systems The insider threat program, built with HR, Legal, and IT Automation and agentic AI that extends analyst capacity (the analyst always owns the decision) Security integration of acquired companies and new environments into EDB's standards Close partnership with IT and Product leadership to build preventive controls into the platforms, pipelines, and products they own, plus security input to third-party risk and device posture with GRC Scaling the program: the org design, operating rhythms, roadmap, budget, and vendor strategy that let coverage grow with the business without growing linearly with headcount What you will bring: 5+ years of management experience leading security teams 7+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, detection, or security engineering A track record of scaling a security function through rapid growth (hiring, automation, and operating discipline), not just running one Strategic thinking that goes beyond the immediate scope of the role The ability to translate technical risk into business impact for executives, legal, customers, and your IT and Product counterparts Comfort in a global, remote-first environment with flexible schedules and on-call responsibilities What will give you an edge: Hands-on scripting or automation experience (Python, Go, etc.) Experience applying AI or agent-based automation to security workflows Cloud security experience and background in M&A security integration Experience building an insider threat or identity assurance program EDB is committed to supporting our employees' overall well being by offering a range of benefits and resources to promote a healthy work-life balance and wellness. We provide access to CuraLinc to aid employees in health and wellness tips and practices, as well as Wellness Fridays extending to December 2026! Check out our career site for more information on perks and benefits and reach out to our Talent Acquisition team for region specific benefits. title: Bilingual Customer Experience Specialist (Spanish)

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. We partner closely with cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, and Operations to surface insights from the front line, reduce friction in the customer journey, and shape future roadmaps. We deliver empathetic, high-quality support through a blend of data-driven, operational excellence. By focusing on clear communication, critical thinking, and continuous improvement, we ensure that every customer interaction not only resolves the immediate issue but also consistently enhances the overall Instacart experience. We are currently hiring for a variety of shifts, including mid-day, and evening coverage, to ensure we provide seamless service throughout the day. Schedule flexibility—including availability for evenings, weekends, and holidays—is essential to meeting the diverse needs of our community. Handle live customer contacts (phone, chat, and/or email) for up to 100% of your scheduled time, consistently delivering clear, empathetic, and efficient support. Navigate and execute complex workflows using established tools, policies, and knowledge base content to resolve a wide range of order and account issues. Resolve edge cases by carefully following documented procedures, seeking guidance when needed, and escalating to the appropriate teams when issues fall outside standard paths. Conduct thorough investigations into customer issues—reviewing account history, order details, and prior interactions—to ensure accurate and fair outcomes. Create internal transfer tickets and document cases with clear, detailed notes so downstream teams have the context they need to resolve issues efficiently. Proactively identify patterns, pain points, and process gaps in day-to-day work, and provide concrete suggestions and recommendations to supervisors and pillar leadership. Act as a positive team player and informal leader by modeling best practices, sharing tips and insights with peers, and contributing to a supportive, inclusive team environment. Surface emerging issues and operational challenges (such as tooling bugs, policy ambiguities, or contact spikes) to leadership quickly and with clear examples, helping the team respond and adapt in real time. About You Minimum qualifications High school diploma or equivalent (some college or specialized training a plus) 1+ year in a customer-facing role (support, retail, hospitality, call center, etc.) with a track record of strong service Fluency in Spanish, both spoken and written Comfort handling live contacts for most of the day (phone, chat, and/or email) in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including clear documentation of cases and transfers, attention to detail and ability to follow established workflows Problem-solving mindset with the ability to investigate issues, interpret account/order details, and make sound judgments within policy Emotional intelligence and resilience when dealing with upset or frustrated customers and complex situations Basic technical proficiency (navigating multiple systems, CRM tools, browser-based applications, and common productivity tools like Google Workspace) Schedule flexibility to support evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs Comfort working with AI-assisted tools and willingness to adopt new technologies that enhance customer support workflows and drive efficiency Preferred qualifications Experience in a contact center or multi-channel support environment (phone + chat + email) Prior exposure to complex, policy-heavy workflows (e.g., financial services, logistics, e‑commerce, or marketplaces) Familiarity with CRM and contact center tools (Salesforce, Genesys/Ujet, Zendesk, etc.) Demonstrated experience surfacing trends or issues to leadership and proposing improvements Proven ability to work collaboratively on a team, share best practices, and provide peer support or informal mentorship Work Schedule Full-time | 40 hours per week Operations run 7 days a week | 7:00 AM – 11:00 PM EST / 4:00 AM – 8:00 PM PST Shift assignments are based on business needs. Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and holidays is required. #LI-Remote Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. title: Consultant Relations Senior Manager
description: Who are we and why should you join us? BetterHelp is on a mission to remove the traditional barriers to therapy and make mental health care more accessible to everyone. Founded in 2013, we are now the world’s largest online therapy service, providing affordable and convenient therapy across the globe. Our network of over 30,000 licensed therapists has helped millions of people take ownership of their mental health and change their lives forever. And we’re not stopping there – as the unmet need for mental health services continues to grow, BetterHelp is committed to being part of the solution. As the Consultant Relations Senior Manager at BetterHelp, you’ll join a diverse team of licensed clinicians, engineers, product pros, creatives, marketers, and business leaders who share a passion for expanding access to therapy. And as a mental health company, we take employee mental health just as seriously as we do our mission. We deeply invest in our team’s well-being and professional development, because we know that business and individual growth go hand-in-hand. At BetterHelp, you’ll carve your own path, make an immediate impact, and be challenged every day – with a supportive community behind you the whole way. What are we looking for? BetterHelp is looking for a Consultant Relations Senior Manager to help accelerate the growth of our Enterprise business by building and activating relationships across the employee benefits broker and consultant ecosystem. In this role, you’ll own broker and consultant engagement across assigned markets, identifying the firms, offices, and individual relationships with the greatest potential to expand BetterHelp’s reach and generate new business opportunities. You’ll build trusted relationships, develop and execute engagement strategies, and help brokers and consultants understand, evaluate, and confidently introduce BetterHelp to their clients. We’re looking for a relationship-driven, commercially minded professional who understands how influence works within the employee benefits ecosystem. You know how to operate at both the organizational level, through enablement, programming, events, and go-to-market initiatives, and the individual level, by developing trusted relationships and credibility with brokers and consultants. You’ll have meaningful autonomy in determining where to focus your efforts, how to activate relationships, and how to translate partner engagement into measurable business impact. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Sales, you’ll use market intelligence, partner insights, internal data, and strong relationship-building skills to identify opportunities, generate pipeline, and strengthen BetterHelp’s position within the employee benefits market. What will you do? Own Broker & Consultant Relationships Build and nurture strong, trust-based relationships with employee benefits brokers, consultants, and other trusted advisors across assigned markets. Independently identify and prioritize the firms, offices, and individual relationships with the greatest potential to influence pipeline, revenue, and market awareness. Develop engagement strategies tailored to individual partners, firms, and markets based on their needs, influence, client base, and potential opportunity. Serve as a primary BetterHelp relationship owner for assigned brokers and consultants, maintaining consistent, high-quality engagement across virtual and in-person interactions. Establish BetterHelp as a trusted behavioral health partner by developing credibility, understanding partner needs, and delivering a strong and responsive partner experience. title: Director, Legal
description: At Submittable, we are transforming how organizations create social impact. Our platform empowers thousands of mission-driven organizations, from nonprofits to government entities, to make a difference in their communities and beyond. In 2024, our innovative software helped organizations worldwide run 30,000 programs , welcomed 1.2 million applicants , and facilitated the distribution of more than $10 billion in funding through our products on behalf of our clients. We are on a mission to help organizations accelerate their impact, so we are proud to partner with organizations focused on Equity & Social Justice, Children & Education, Creative & Arts, Health & Wellness, Economic Justice & Opportunity, and Environment & Climate. At Submittable, technology and purpose converge, offering a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful change. About the Role Submittable is hiring a Director, Legal to lead our legal function as we scale our SaaS business. You'll be a hands-on legal leader, responsible for day-to-day legal operations, the legal team, and the policies and processes that let Submittable grow with confidence. You'll manage the legal team and serve as a primary resource on privacy law, customer contract negotiation, and product and technology intellectual property matters, while also advising on the broader range of legal issues a growing SaaS company faces. This role reports to the CFO and works closely with teams across the organization and with the executive leadership team. What You’ll Do Lead the day-to-day legal function, setting priorities and standards for how legal work gets done across the company. Build, manage, and mentor a legal team, including hiring, workload distribution, and professional development. Serve as a primary resource on data privacy and security law (e.g., GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other U.S. and international privacy regimes), including policy development and incident response. Negotiate customer contracts, including MSAs, order forms, DPAs, and enterprise procurement paperwork, balancing legal risk against deal velocity. Advise Product and Engineering on intellectual property matters, including IP ownership, licensing, open-source usage, and protection of proprietary technology. Partner with Sales and Revenue Operations to maintain contracting playbooks, standard terms, and approval thresholds that let deals move quickly without unnecessary escalation. Manage outside counsel relationships and legal spend across litigation, IP, and specialty areas. Advise company leadership on governance, risk, and compliance matters, escalating to the executive team as needed. Support employment law matters in partnership with People/HR, including policy review and workplace investigations as needed. Monitor the regulatory and legislative landscape relevant to SaaS, data privacy, artificial intelligence, and the sectors Submittable serves, and translate changes into practical guidance for the business. Manage the contract lifecycle management approach and legal operations tooling. Collaborate with the Finance team to address and collect overdue customer accounts, utilizing escalation procedures and legal remedies as appropriate. Establish and track key performance indicators for the Legal department to assess progress and fuel continuous process improvement, including the integration of AI-driven workflow automation. Support M&A, corporate transactions, and other strategic initiatives as they arise. What We’re Looking For J.D. and active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state. 8+ years of legal experience, including at least 3 years in-house at a B2B SaaS or technology company. Private equity-backed experience is a plus. At least 3 years of hands-on experience negotiating SaaS customer contracts, including MSAs, DPAs, and complex order forms. Experience managing or mentoring attorneys and legal professionals, with an interest in building and growing a legal team. Strong expertise in data privacy and security law, with hands-on experience supporting privacy programs and responding to regulatory change. Solid grounding in intellectual property law as it applies to software products, including licensing and open-source considerations. Experience advising business and senior leaders on governance, risk, and compliance matters. Sound business judgment and the ability to balance legal risk with commercial pragmatism. Excellent negotiation, communication, and cross-functional influence skills. Demonstrated ability to build and improve legal processes and policy in a fast-growing organization. Location: This is a remote, U.S.-based role — you must live and reside in the U.S. full-time. Salary Details: The annual salary range for this position is $180,000 - $225,000. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. We also have a location-based compensation structure; there may be a different range for candidates in other locations. We are interested in every qualified candidate eligible to work in the United States; however, we cannot accommodate scholastic or employment visas at this time . In addition, we are not able to consider applicants who reside in the following states: Alaska, Delaware, Hawaii, Louisiana, Maine, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, West Virginia, and Wyoming. Fraudulent Recruitment Advisory : Submittable will NEVER request bank details, payment, or personal information during the hiring process, nor extend offers without an interview. All legitimate communications come from official submittable.com email addresses. If you receive suspicious outreach, please report it to people@submittable.com . (Please do not submit applications, resumes, cover letters, or other candidacy materials to this email address. Emails of this nature will not be reviewed or considered.) Why Submittable? Joining Submittable means becoming part of a forward-thinking, mission-driven company that values innovation, collaboration, and growth. We empower organizations working for social good with technology that accelerates their work, amplifies their impact, and drives meaningful change. At Submittable, you’ll find a supportive, dynamic work environment where your contributions directly influence our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment and are excited to be part of a company dedicated to social impact, we invite you to apply! Benefits: We are proud to offer highly competitive benefits to our full-time employees, including: Comprehensive health and life insurance with optional HSA, FSA, and DCA accounts 401(k) plan with employer match starting day one Equity stock options to share in our success Flexible hours, remote work options, and generous vacation and sick leave Paid parental leave for mothers, fathers, and adoptive parents Professional development stipends to support your career growth Opportunities to participate in community outreach and volunteer programs Monthly company-sponsored happy hours and gatherings to connect and unwind Our Commitment to Inclusion & Belonging At Submittable, we believe technology is a force for good, driving social impact and enabling corporate social responsibility on a global scale. To achieve this, we are committed to fostering a workplace that values inclusion and belonging as central pillars of our culture. We embrace the strength of our diverse community by creating a safe space where employees feel empowered to share ideas, celebrate unique experiences, and learn from one another. By prioritizing inclusion, we aim to build an environment where everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and make innovative contributions that enable our customers to tackle complex challenges and spread more good. As a globally used platform, we are dedicated to hiring and supporting employees who represent a range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. This includes diversity in ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender, religion, ability, culture, and socioeconomic background. About Our Process Our goal is a fair, efficient, and thorough evaluation process that benefits you and our team and respects your time. As you can imagine, we have received a high volume of applications. Your willingness to participate in I.D. Verification and answer a few questions early allows us to move through the process more quickly. We are committed to leveraging AI technologies responsibly, ensuring their use is equitable, fair and safe. To ensure fairness and accurate skill assessment, we do not allow the use of AI tools (including note takers, transcription tools, or recordings) during take home tests or interviews. If you have questions or need accommodations, please let us know. For additional information and guidance on using AI to prepare an interview at Submittable, please click here . We believe our approach streamlines the hiring process and respects your time by ensuring that every conversation is substantive and focused on your unique qualifications. We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to learning more about you.

title: Assistant General Counsel, Servicing
description: About GoodLeap: GoodLeap is a technology company delivering best-in-class financing and software products for sustainable solutions, from solar panels and batteries to energy-efficient HVAC, heat pumps, roofing, windows, and more. Over 1 million homeowners have benefited from our simple, fast, and frictionless technology that makes the adoption of these products more affordable, accessible, and easier to understand. Thousands of professionals deploying home efficiency and solar solutions rely on GoodLeap’s proprietary, AI-powered applications and developer tools to drive more transparent customer communication, deeper business intelligence, and streamlined payment and operations. Our platform has led to more than $30 billion in financing for sustainable solutions since 2018. GoodLeap is also proud to support our award-winning nonprofit, GivePower, which is building and deploying life-saving water and clean electricity systems, changing the lives of more than 1.6 million people across Africa, Asia, and South America. The Assistant General Counsel, Servicing will report to the Deputy General Counsel, Executive Vice President, and will serve as the dedicated legal resource for GoodLeap’s Servicing Team. This role is designed for a practicing attorney with deep, practical experience in consumer loan and mortgage loan servicing and collections law and who can provide real-time operational guidance to the Servicing organization. The Assistant General Counsel will provide daily support to the Servicing Team, advise on loss mitigation programs, collections strategy, default management and regulatory compliance, and will be the go-to legal representative for matters affecting serviced loan portfolios, customer communications, and servicing operations. Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities: Lead compliance analysis and policy development under Reg X (RESPA), Reg Z (TILA), FDCPA, UDAAP, TCPA, etc. and applicable state servicing and collections laws, GSE and agency servicing guidelines. Draft, review, and maintain loss mitigation policies, collections strategies, and servicing procedures, ensuring alignment with regulatory obligations, procedural requirements and investor obligations. Identify, assess, and mitigate legal and regulatory risks and advise on structuring for current and new investment products and strategies to ensure compliance with applicable laws. Monitor regulatory developments and advise on implementation of new rules affecting servicing and collections operations. Review and negotiate vendor contracts and SOWs supporting collections and default management functions (e.g., third-party collectors, BPO servicers, foreclosure counsel). Partner with Capital Markets and Portfolio Management on servicing representations, covenants, and compliance requirements in asset sale and securitization transactions. Support regulatory examination management and respond to consumer complaints escalated through CFPB, state agencies, or litigation channels. Required Skills, Knowledge and Abilities: Minimum 10 years of experience as a practicing attorney, with substantial time spent in consumer loan servicing, collections or default management — ideally including in-house experience at a consumer finance and/or mortgage servicer or subservicer, GSE/agency approved seller-servicer and/or consumer finance lender. Deep working knowledge of servicing and consumer debt collections laws and practice and applicable state collections and foreclosure laws (e.g., FDCPA, TCPA, FCRA, UDAAP, TILA, RESPA, ECOA, etc.) and related title and lien resolution issues. Demonstrated experience advising on loss mitigation structuring and post-default strategy in a consumer finance, mortgage finance and/or home improvement lending context. Fluency in FDCPA and TCPA compliance for collections outreach, state collections licensing requirements and regulatory classification of collections operations. Familiarity with AI governance and emerging regulatory frameworks applicable to AI use in collections and financial services operations. Proven ability to deliver clear, operationally actionable legal guidance and to own and stand behind a legal position in a fast-paced business environment. Membership in applicable state bar in good standing. Juris Doctor degree from an ABA accredited law school. Able to juggle multiple workstreams under tight deadlines. Clear writing and verbal communication with business professionals and counsel. History of working well with business professionals, and with cross-functional teams (internal and external). Compensation Additional Information Compensation: $240,000–$260,000 annually Additional Information Regarding Job Duties and Job Descriptions: Job duties include additional responsibilities as assigned by one's supervisor or other managers related to the position/department. This job description is meant to describe the general nature and level of work being performed; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and other skills required for the position. The Company reserves the right at any time with or without notice to alter or change job responsibilities, reassign or transfer job position or assign additional job responsibilities, subject to applicable law. The Company shall provide reasonable accommodations of known disabilities to enable a qualified applicant or employee to apply for employment, perform the essential functions of the job, or enjoy the benefits and privileges of employment as required by the law. If you are an extraordinary professional who thrives in a collaborative work culture and values a rewarding career, then we want to work with you! Apply today! We are committed to protecting your privacy. To learn more about how we collect, use, and safeguard your personal information during the application process, please review our Employment Privacy Policy and Recruiting Policy on AI .

description: Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey. The Pulsar team builds platform and admin services that all Bloomreach SaaS products rely on. In your first year, you’ll develop features used by thousands of customers and deliver fast, consistent, and high-energy (but low-drama) product releases. We all work remotely from the US, India, and Europe. Examples of our services: Central services to publish Model Context Protocol APIs for external AI agents Multi-product customer provisioning and licensing orchestration Integrated user management, authentication, and authorization High-availability, centralized configuration management Tools for new customer integration & product tuning Why you’ll love your work Technical Variety: Cloud-native services with diverse tech stacks offer learning and experimentation. Impact: Our services are used by customers and teams across the company – engineers, product managers, services consultants, and even executives. Autonomy: Senior engineers design, build, and deploy complete projects and are experts in our services. Teamwork: Your teammates are also high performers and will support you with learning our systems, brainstorming & design review, and running high-reliability production deployments. Your typical day Your day begins with review of a teammate’s GitLab merge request. It has already been reviewed by Claude, but you’ll think deeply about the business problem, alternative solutions, and future needs. Then you spend a few undisturbed hours “in the flow,” working on a technical design doc for a new project. Once you’ve completed a draft, you send it to another teammate for feedback, then decide to jump on a Zoom call to talk it over and refine it. After lunch, you join the team for a quick standup via Zoom to discuss current work and the plan for the next few days. You mention that you’re finishing up a small improvement to improve the logging and alerting for one of our components that requires high uptime. A teammate offers to review your changes. It has some complex behavior, so you walk through it together and make a few improvements. Soon, the new unit tests are green. With a few keystrokes, you create a merge request, spin up a dev instance, and deploy your change. After some quick smoke tests, you and your teammate decide to merge the change. Your improvement will be deployed in production with the release in a few days. Next, you respond to a Slack request for advice on integrating with the authorization API. You draft a short tech design doc that links the API spec, code examples, and optimization tips. You discuss it on the team channel, and your manager forwards it to another team that’s also starting a new service. Your day ends with a chat with a product manager about questions that came up while drafting the tech design. With their feedback, you refine the proposal to deliver the core feature more quickly, while the product manager will work with customers and decide how much more to invest. Tomorrow, you’ll break down the tasks in Jira and decide what you’ll complete yourself and what you’ll ask teammates to complete…. Drive: Rapidly ship product improvements that affect thousands of users in a low-drama and high-trust way. Security & Reliability: Balance risks and benefits of change with discipline and agility. Communication: Organize technical work and maintain trust/respect across multiple teams, geographic regions, and departments. Knowledge Sharing: Proactively share expertise, guide less experienced team members, and document work for long-term sustainability. title: Full Stack Software Engineer
description: Who are we and why should you join us? BetterHelp is on a mission to champion the well-being in all of us. We’re working to make mental healthcare more accessible, so more people can get the support they need, when they need it. As the world’s largest online therapy service, we’ve connected millions of people with a network of more than 30,000 licensed therapists-- and we’re not stopping there. As the unmet need for mental health services continues to grow, BetterHelp is committed to being part of the solution. As a Full Stack Software Engineer at BetterHelp, you’ll join a diverse team of clinicians, engineers, product pros, creatives, marketers, and business leaders who share a passion for expanding access to therapy. You’ll have the opportunity to make an immediate impact, grow alongside the business, and do meaningful work alongside people who care deeply about what we’re building together. What are we looking for? We're looking for a talented software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, learning continuously, and building products that make a meaningful difference. This role is ideal for someone who has delivered multiple challenging projects, takes pride in writing thoughtful, maintainable code, and enjoys both mentoring and learning from teammates. You'll join an engineering culture that values ownership, curiosity, collaboration, and sound technical judgment. We embrace modern engineering practices and thoughtfully adopt new technologies, including AI, to help engineers focus on solving hard problems while keeping human expertise at the center of every decision. What technologies will you work with? We use a mix of established and modern technologies to support a platform serving millions of users. As our products evolve, we're continually improving our architecture, modernizing portions of our codebase, and evaluating technologies that help us build secure, reliable, and scalable software. Backend: Linux, nginx, Laravel (PHP), MySQL, Redis Frontend: React, Next.js, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS/SASS Existing technologies you may encounter as we modernize the platform: Twig, Bootstrap, jQuery We do not expect candidates to have worked with every technology in our environment. We value strong software engineering fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems. What will you do? You will develop end to end, owning features from technical design and development through deployment, monitoring, and continued improvement. You will write clean, secure, readable, maintainable, and scalable code. You will collaborate closely with engineers, product managers, designers, and other cross-functional partners. You will design, integrate, and build internal and external APIs. You will develop new products and features while improving and modernizing existing systems. You will write and optimize SQL queries and design relational database schemas. You will create and maintain complex backend services and algorithms. You will profile, troubleshoot, and optimize new and legacy code. You will build experiences that work across mobile, tablet, and desktop environments. You will contribute to code reviews, technical discussions, and engineering practices that improve quality, reliability, security, and developer experience. You will ship thoughtfully and frequently in an agile environment with continuous deployment. You will care about our product, mission, and long-term success, well beyond checking off development tasks. You will thoughtfully use approved AI-assisted development tools to reduce repetitive work, explore solutions, and improve productivity while applying your own engineering judgment to architecture, implementation, security, privacy, and code quality. Engineers remain accountable for every technical decision. What will you NOT do? You will NOT worry about funding. We have startup energy, with the support and resources of our parent company, Teladoc Health. You will NOT be limited to a narrow set of responsibilities. We encourage employees to contribute ideas, develop new skills, collaborate across teams, and explore opportunities that support both their growth and the growing needs of the business. You will NOT be expected to navigate a culture driven by ego or unnecessary hierarchy. We value respectful collaboration, thoughtful debate, and teammates who are committed to shared success. You will NOT be expected to sacrifice your well-being to make an impact. We work hard and hold ourselves to high standards, all while supporting sustainable ways of working. You will NOT have to wonder why your work matters. The work we do here helps to expand access to mental health care and supports people seeking help when they need it. Can I work remotely? Yes. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in the U.S. While we embrace the flexibility of remote work, we also value opportunities to bring teams together in person for collaboration and connection. BetterHelp covers approved expenses for company-requested travel, and reasonable accommodations are available for employees who are unable to travel. Requirements Must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Deep understanding of web development concepts and principles. Examples of full-stack projects or significant product features. At least one major demonstrable project that includes frontend code, backend code, and a database. Ability to design, develop, and launch a web application or substantial feature from start to finish. Ability to learn quickly, navigate an established codebase, and build new skills independently. A strong sense of ownership and eagerness to build something meaningful. Five or more years of professional web development experience in any stack, solving challenging problems and implementing new features from scratch. Three or more years of experience with SQL, including relational schema design and complex queries. Familiarity with web application, data, and SQL security best practices. Comfort working outside the abstractions of a framework and understanding what is happening behind the scenes. Experience using Git in a collaborative team environment. Sound engineering judgment and a thoughtful approach to modern development tools, including AI assistants, with appropriate attention to security, privacy, and code quality. Bonus (Helpful, but not required) Experience working with PHP, Laravel, or the LAMP/LEMP ecosystem. Experience with React or Next.js. Experience modernizing established applications or incrementally replacing legacy systems. Experience working in a startup, growth-stage company, or other fast-moving environment. Experience building products in health care, mental health, or another highly regulated or privacy-sensitive field. Experience mentoring or supporting the growth of other engineers. title: Customer Success Manager
description: Customer Success Manager Remote | North America About Hubstaff Hubstaff helps organizations around the world optimize productivity and workforce operations. We’ve been a remote-first company for over a decade — and we’re on a mission to help distributed teams work smarter, not harder. The Role We’re hiring a Customer Success Manager (NAMER) to own the customer journey end to end — ensuring rapid activation, long-term adoption, retention, and expansion of Hubstaff across a portfolio of ~150 mid-market and Enterprise customers across North and South America. Your focus will span Onboarding, Adoption, Retention, Expansion, Renewal, Billing, and Escalations , ensuring every customer achieves measurable outcomes and lasting value from Hubstaff. Lead live onboarding sessions, follow-ups, and check-ins to ensure customers realize time-to-value quickly. Manage ongoing customer relationships — conduct value-driven business reviews, track progress toward customer goals, and proactively drive retention and growth across your book of business. Be directly responsible for Gross and Net Revenue Retention (GRR & NRR) across your book of business. Manage renewals and the associated process, expansion opportunities, and at-risk accounts, ensuring Hubstaff’s customers are retained and setup to grow with us. Build and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with key decision-makers and daily users, becoming their advocate and advisor. Deliver key account insights : report on customer health, renewal risk, and expansion opportunities to the wider Hubstaff leadership team. Develop scalable processes and playbooks that streamline onboarding and lifecycle management, contributing to a continuously improving Customer Success practice. Use data to drive action : monitor product adoption metrics, health and associated alerts, feature usage, and engagement data to identify risk or opportunity, and implement targeted success plans. Educate and enable customers through webinars, product walkthroughs, and resources that increase confidence, adoption, and satisfaction. Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Support, and Engineering teams to resolve issues quickly, advocate for customer feedback, and influence roadmap decisions. Continuously experiment and iterate : test engagement approaches, refine playbooks, and share learnings to enhance customer outcomes and internal efficiency. What You’ll Bring 4+ years of experience in Customer Success within a PLG SaaS company. Proven experience managing 100+ accounts , balancing proactive engagement with operational efficiency. Strong ownership mentality — you’re accountable for your customers’ results and take initiative to solve problems before they escalate. Exceptional relationship and communication skills , able to engage both executive and operational stakeholders with credibility and empathy. Comfortable working with data, dashboards, and customer metrics to inform decisions and drive performance. Experience influencing renewal, retention, and expansion outcomes , ideally in a PLG or subscription-based SaaS model. Familiarity with tools such as Vitally, HubSpot, Slack, and Stripe is a plus. Self-motivated, comfortable working autonomously in a distributed team , and energized by a high-growth, evolving environment. Compensation & Bonus The base salary for this role is $80,000–$100,000 annually , plus the opportunity to earn additional compensation through a quarterly performance bonus. Our bonus plan rewards your impact on customer success, with incentives tied to customer retention and expansion goals. Why You’ll Love Working at Hubstaff Fully remote role with flexible working hours Meaningful work — you’ll help thousands of teams operate more effectively and sustainably every day Supportive culture built on trust, autonomy, and balance Private health insurance, paid time off, and local benefits (for employees) Annual stipends for home office, wellness, or professional development Clear career progression pathways, mentorship opportunities, and skill development programs Global company retreats in unique destinations, co nnecting our remote team in person Inclusion at Hubstaff We welcome and celebrate diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. Everyone deserves to feel valued and supported — and we’re committed to creating an inclusive environment for all.

Apply dielines, manage file layers, and prepare files for various print and production formats. Convert Figma layouts into production-ready assets with precision and consistency. Serve as the final quality check before anything goes to print, catching every detail, every time. Production Management Ensure all production files meet vendor specifications, color standards, and substrate requirements, with working familiarity of U.S.-based print production environments and expectations. Maintain the highest design quality standards, including alignment, proportions, margins, and overall layout precision; every file should be pixel-perfect. Support proofing, pre-press, and press check processes with attention to detail and accuracy. Collaborate with internal and external production teams to troubleshoot and problem-solve, with a strong ability to do so asynchronously across time zones when needed. Maintain clarity on active vs. released files and ensure stakeholders are always working with the most up-to-date materials. Templates & Resources Create and maintain production templates, dieline guides, and reference materials. Contribute to documentation and onboarding resources to support team efficiency and alignment across geographies. Asset Maintenance & Workflow Ownership Manage ongoing brand font rollout across packaging, collateral, and print templates. Support the design and production of brand magazines and printed collateral. Maintain artwork consistency across assets and ensure alignment with evolving brand guidelines. Team Collaboration & Culture Own the production design process. Proactively seek out opportunities to contribute, think ahead, and take initiative, don't wait to be asked; step in where you see a need. Work closely with graphic designers to uphold creative intent through production. Partner with structural, industrial, and CMF designers to ensure graphics align with physical form. Collaborate with marketing, ops, and supply chain teams when needed. Communicate proactively and with transparency, keeping U.S.-based teammates informed and aligned regardless of time zone differences. You Have 12+ years of experience in print and packaging production design. Expert-level proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, InDesign, Photoshop). Strong working knowledge of Figma and the ability to translate digital designs into print-ready files. Deep understanding of print production, packaging materials, color management, and dielines — including familiarity with U.S.-based print standards and vendor workflows. Experience managing system updates such as fonts and templates across large sets of files. Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and quality. A keen eye for layout, typography, and consistency. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; you take pride in clean files and clear systems. Experience working directly with vendors, printers, and packaging suppliers. Comfort with flexible scheduling, asynchronous communication, and the self-direction required to thrive in a remote, cross-time-zone environment.
